sections.overview: Biotodoma wavrini is a South American geophagine cichlid known from the Orinoco and Negro river systems. Its genus also includes B. cupido, whose breeding biology is better documented.
sections.identification: It is a small, elongated eartheater with iridescent blue cheek spots and a flank blotch set lower and farther forward than in B. cupido. Like other eartheaters, it sifts sediment through the gills to retain edible particles.
sections.habitat: Records place it in the upper and middle Orinoco and Negro basins, including tributaries and quiet margins with sand or leaf litter. Accounts describe both clear-water streams and soft, acidic blackwater habitats.
sections.diet: It takes small benthic invertebrates and organic material while sorting bottom sediment. A comparative dietary study found benthic invertebrates alongside variable detritus in this species.
sections.behavior: It forages close to the bottom by taking and expelling mouthfuls of substrate. Aquarium observations describe territorial activity near possible spawning sites, but not a complete breeding account.
sections.reproduction: The spawning method of B. wavrini remains poorly documented. Biparental substrate spawning is known in its congener B. cupido, but should not be treated as confirmed for B. wavrini.
sections.ecology: As a bottom-feeding fish, it participates in the turnover of small invertebrates and detritus in river margins. Its reported habitats span more than one water type, so it is not established as an obligate blackwater species.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted here do not establish a current global threat category for this species. Distribution records and reproductive uncertainty are better documented than population trends.
